blockers.title: raw and selected truncated together at an endpoint still passes
blockers.basis: Demonstrated by reverting the receiving logic to pre-fix and observing acceptance, then observing rejection on current. Not inferred from the presence of gate code.
evidence: Pre-fix module lifted via: git show 73dca01d0:experiments/k528/k528_nfp_event_study.py > /tmp/k528_prefix/k528_nfp_event_study.py
grep -c LATEST_OBSERVED_RELEASE_DAY_OF_MONTH -> pre-fix 0, current 7; grep -c absent_required -> pre-fix 0, current 4. The endpoint check did not exist before 17f12d16c.

Current test suite run against the PRE-FIX module: 14 failed in 0.59s (all fail at _load_gate: "could not lift ['LATEST_OBSERVED_RELEASE_DAY_OF_MONTH']"). This proves the tests are coupled to the new logic, but it is a harness-level failure, so I did not stop here.

Sharper probe (/tmp/k528_probe.py) - same B2 attack fed to both gate versions directly, lifting only the gate function and the constants it reads: PRE-FIX 73dca01d0 -> head: ACCEPTED (deleted 2005-01; raw=259 selected=253; head_shortfall=34d tail_shortfall=21d); tail: ACCEPTED (deleted 2026-03; raw=259 selected=253; head_shortfall=6d tail_shortfall=44d). POST-FIX 17f12d16c -> head: RAISED ('the requested window 2005-01-01..2026-03-27 fully contains the publication window of 1 month(s) that the calendar has no release for: [2005-01]'); tail: RAISED (same, naming [2026-03]).

The probe independently reproduces Codex's own numbers verbatim - 259 raw / 253 selected, head shortfall 34d, tail shortfall 44d - which is an external check that the attack I ran is the attack Codex described.
Current suite on current code: 24 passed in 2.43s (test_k528_completeness_gate.py + test_k528_price_coverage_gate.py).

Anti-vacuity is built in, verified by reading: test_k528_completeness_gate.py:258-275 (test_endpoint_truncation_is_invisible_without_the_new_check) disables ONLY the new check, leaves every prior defence intact, and asserts the truncated calendar is ACCEPTED. _load_gate:126-133 asserts each mutation applies exactly once and refuses to report a green run otherwise.

test_k528_completeness_gate.py:277-292 pins the property that makes the gate work - required months derive from the REQUESTED window, not the observed feed (narrowing the window changes the requirement; truncating the feed does not).
blockers.notes: This is the strongest of the four. The gate is measured against the requested window, which a truncated feed cannot move, so it is not feed-checking-feed. The remaining hole (declare a month in KNOWN_MISSING_MONTHS AND delete it from raw) is disclosed in remediation unresolved[0] and is a documented-false-claim threat model, not silent truncation - I agree that is a different and lesser class.

blockers.title: price data tail truncation does not fail closed
blockers.basis: Gate bodies read line by line for fail-open, then exercised with deliberately deficient inputs.
evidence: experiments/k528/k528_nfp_event_study.py:505-537 check_price_coverage - raises on empty frame and on head/tail shortfall beyond MAX_PRICE_COVERAGE_SHORTFALL_DAYS (10d). Called unconditionally at :541-542 for both SPY and ^VIX at module level; no try/except, no default, no flag to skip.

k528_nfp_event_study.py:554-590 check_vix_forward_fill_age - measures the longest NaN run BEFORE filling, raises if > MAX_VIX_FFILL_TRADING_DAYS (3, :159), and raises again if any NaN survives the ffill (start-of-sample gap). Called unconditionally at :592.

k528_nfp_event_study.py:655-662 - 'if unmapped: raise'. n_outside_price_sample is now forced to zero rather than reported and ignored; the comment at :647-654 states why the earlier design boundary no longer applies once both endpoints are verified.

Empirical probe (/tmp/k528_b3_probe.py), current gates, tolerance price=10d vix_ffill=3d: SPY tail short 1 month -> BLOCKED; SPY head short 1 month -> BLOCKED; empty download -> BLOCKED ('download returned no rows'); VIX missing 20 consecutive sessions -> BLOCKED ('the limit is 3'); VIX missing at sample start -> BLOCKED ('nothing to carry forward').

Negative controls in the same probe correctly ACCEPT: full window, tail short 8 days (inside 10d tolerance), VIX missing 2 sessions (holiday). A gate that raises on everything would have failed these - it did not, so the blocks above are discriminating, not indiscriminate.

Fail-open sweep: grep -nE 'try:|except|suppress|fallback' over the whole script returns 6 hits, all accounted for - :172-181 is temp-file cleanup inside write_json_atomic and re-raises on line 182 (the original error is not swallowed); :472 is a comment stating the calendar loader deliberately has no except branch; :187 and :1713 are comments/metadata ('fallback: none'). There is no exception handler anywhere in the analysis path.
blockers.notes: Both guards were extracted into named functions specifically so a test can attack them; the script comment at :566-568 states the reasoning ('an unexercised guard and an absent guard fail the same way'), and test_k528_price_coverage_gate.py (10 tests) does exercise them. I confirmed the behaviour independently rather than relying on that suite.

blockers.title: no multiple-comparison family declared while claiming 5% significance
blockers.scope_of_failure: The statistical content is correct and complete. Two problems remain: (a) the literal dispatch criterion - family defined BEFORE the rerun - is not met and cannot be met retroactively; (b) one sanctioned phrasing in README contradicts the artifact's own pre-registration disclosure.
what_passes: Complete Holm lists for BOTH families, including every failing test - not only the survivors. confirmatory_family n=6: A 0.1121/0.1121 (fails), B 0.02085/0.04170 (survives), C 0.00194/0.00582, E_pearson 1.98e-13/1.19e-12, E_spearman 1.67e-08/6.68e-08, H 4.55e-09/2.28e-08. all_outputs_family n=22: every one listed, B 0.02085 -> p_holm 0.37533 (does NOT survive), plus all 12 G_month entries and D/F/I/J at p_holm 1.0 or 0.398.
These reproduce Codex's own indicative figures (~0.0417 confirmatory, ~0.375 all-outputs) to 3 significant figures, which is an independent cross-check on the correction arithmetic.

multiplicity.pre_registered = false, with pre_registration_note stating plainly: 'Not pre-registered. The confirmatory endpoints predate the date correction and this rerun, but were not lodged before the data were seen.'
README.md:193-198 presents all three readings side by side (nominal 0.0209 reject / Holm-6 0.0417 reject / Holm-22 0.375 DO NOT reject) rather than quoting only the favourable one.

The mechanical family stamp claimed in the commit message is real and does raise: k528_nfp_event_study.py:1912 _JSON_KEY_TO_FAMILY_NAME, applied at :1945-1952, with :1977-1984 collecting unstamped entries and raising RuntimeError ('A new test was added without being placed in a family'). Verified by reading the code path, not the commit message.

timing_evidence_requested_by_dispatch.family_definition_first_appears: 17f12d16c (2026-07-20 12:54:55) - git log -S 'confirmatory_family' and -S 'B_nfp_vs_friday_welch' over the script each return exactly one commit: 17f12d16c. The family definition therefore POSTDATES the rerun by ~26 hours.
timing_evidence_requested_by_dispatch.endpoints_first_appear: 461d23ae4 (2026-04-18 15:43:05), three months BEFORE the rerun. Verified by extracting that revision of the script and grepping it: ttest_ind(nfp_abs_returns, non_nfp_abs...) x1 (endpoint A), ttest_ind against friday_non_nfp_abs at :209 (endpoint B), mannwhitneyu x1 (C), pearsonr x1 (E), spearmanr x1 (E), ttest_ind(high_vix, low_vix) x1 (H). All six confirmatory endpoints existed pre-rerun.
timing_evidence_requested_by_dispatch.conclusion: The agent's claim 'the six endpoints predate the rerun' is TRUE and git-verifiable. The dispatch's stricter criterion - that the FAMILY DEFINITION predate the rerun - is FALSE and is unfixable after the fact. The artifact does not claim otherwise; it sets pre_registered=false. Codex's own minimal fix asked only for 'rerun 前既有的 confirmatory endpoints', which is satisfied.

evidence_of_failure: experiments/k528/README.md:199 - '**這個 family 不是預先登記的，必須講清楚。**' (this family is NOT pre-registered, and that must be stated plainly).

experiments/k528/README.md:203 - four lines later, under 可以寫的 (what you ARE allowed to write): '「nominal 顯著；在事先聲明的六項 confirmatory family 內通過 Holm 校正」'. '事先聲明' means declared in advance. The document therefore licenses a downstream writer to publish a pre-specification claim that the same document, and multiplicity.pre_registered=false, both deny.

This is the same failure mode as B1: the analysis layer is honest, the sanctioned-phrasing layer overclaims. README:203 is the single highest-leverage sentence in the file because it is the one a publishing agent copies.
blockers.what_would_close_it: Delete '事先聲明的' from README:203 (e.g. '在六項 confirmatory family 內通過 Holm 校正（該 family 非預先登記，見上）'). One phrase. The non-pre-registration itself needs no further action - it is correctly disclosed and correctly mitigated by dual reporting, and I do not regard it as independently blocking.

(2) DIRECT GATE PROBE (`uv run python /tmp/k528_probe.py`), which is the decisive one because it bypasses the harness and exercises the gate itself: `=== PRE-FIX 73dca01d0 === 端點常數存在: False | head: ACCEPTED (刪掉 2005-01; raw=259 selected=253; head_shortfall=34d tail_shortfall=21d) | tail: ACCEPTED (刪掉 2026-03; raw=259 selected=253; head_shortfall=6d tail_shortfall=44d)`. Both endpoint truncations sail through, matching Codex's independent reproduction exactly.
b2_adversarial_demonstration.post_fix_run: (1) SUITE: `uv run --extra dev pytest experiments/k528/test_k528_completeness_gate.py experiments/k528/test_k528_price_coverage_gate.py -q` -> `24 passed in 2.43s`. (2) SAME DIRECT PROBE against 17f12d16c: `=== POST-FIX 17f12d16c === 端點常數存在: True | head: RAISED -> 'the requested window 2005-01-01..2026-03-27 fully contains the publication window of 1 month(s) that the calendar has no release for: [2005-01]' | tail: RAISED -> ... [2026-03]`. Both ends now fail closed and the rejection names the vanished month.
b2_adversarial_demonstration.verdict: DEMONSTRATED. The attack is accepted pre-fix and rejected post-fix, with Codex's own diagnostic numbers (259/253, 34d, 44d) reproduced independently.
